# Taksim

Taksim is a local-first sufficiency ledger for AI coding. It reads the local history and hooks of Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot, prices every session, and grades finished turns with an LLM judge to show when a cheaper model would have been enough. It stores metadata only: no prompts, responses, code, paths or credentials.

Canonical site: https://taksim.edgee.tech
Documentation: https://taksim.edgee.tech/docs
Getting started: https://taksim.edgee.tech/docs/getting-started
Sign-in (optional): https://taksim.edgee.tech/docs/sign-in
Pricing: https://taksim.edgee.tech/pricing
Privacy: https://taksim.edgee.tech/privacy

Current client boundary:
- Claude Code (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise subscription): history import, hooks, status line, judging, reports. Observe-only: no proxy and no model changes.
- Claude Code (API key): all of the above, plus optional live routing through the local gateway in sessions launched with `taksim claude`.
- Codex CLI (ChatGPT plan): history import from `CODEX_HOME` sessions, reports. Observe-only. Judging is not supported yet.
- Codex CLI (OpenAI API key): history import, reports, plus optional live routing through the local gateway in sessions launched with `taksim codex`. Judging is not supported yet (only the experimental Jev judge grades these turns, and a single weak judge never counts toward savings).
- GitHub Copilot: usage import from the local Copilot CLI session store, reports; no request-time routing.

Judging covers Claude Code turns only. A verdict counts toward the "could have saved" figure only when two judges agree and at least one is a strong judge.

Usage and cost: API-key usage is shown in billed dollars; subscription usage is shown as API-equivalent list-price dollars, labelled as quota, not billed. Weekly reports are on demand: `taksim report weekly` and `taksim digest`.

Platforms: Windows only.

Release status: the current public release (v0.1.1) is an early preview. Judging, reports, `taksim setup` and the credential check that keeps subscription sign-ins out of the local gateway ship in the next release.

Pricing: the CLI is free for any individual developer, at home or at work. Team is $8 per active developer per month, $99 per month minimum, 20% off with annual billing. The team roll-up is built from exports each developer creates and can inspect before sharing; exports carry repo aliases, never paths.

Sign-in is optional and off by default: install Taksim and run `taksim claude` or `taksim codex` with no account. Hosted sign-in only activates when an operator sets `Identity__Enabled=true`, in which case it supports Google/GitHub browser sign-in and stores device credentials in Windows Credential Manager (up to 24 hours, no automatic refresh). The public installer remains v0.1.1, which predates this opt-in sign-in flow; it currently requires a source/development build.

Everything runs locally on 127.0.0.1 by default; nothing leaves the machine unless you opt in to a hosted Taksim feature or a remote judge on your own key (which receives truncated excerpts of the turns it grades). There is no default hosted routing-advice service. This does not describe the native AI client itself: Claude Code, Codex, and similar clients still send prompts and responses to their own provider under that provider's terms, independent of Taksim.

Subscription traffic is observed, not rewritten: when Claude Code runs on a Claude subscription (Max/Pro, `Authorization: Bearer`), `taksim claude` launches Claude Code natively and observes it from local transcripts and hooks; `taksim report baseline` shows usage and quota, without rewriting the model. Model rewrite applies only to API-key traffic (`x-api-key`), and only in sessions launched through Taksim.
